column2: skipping breakfast because you are in a hurry
column3: eat at least something simple such as toast, fruit or cereal before school
column4: the brain needs food to concentrate and you may feel tired or grumpy by mid-morning

column2: taking the register or roll call
column3: answer clearly when your name is called, for example «here» or «present»
column4: the school must know exactly which children are in the building in case of an emergency

column3: learn which subject comes when and on which days, and check it the night before
column4: you will bring the right things and know where to be

column2: moving between classrooms in the corridor
column3: walk on the correct side, do not run, and keep your voice low
column4: corridors are crowded and running causes collisions and falls

column2: an earthquake drill in New Zealand or the western USA
column3: drop, cover under a desk and hold on until the shaking stops
column4: falling objects cause most injuries and a sturdy desk protects your head

column2: your usual adult does not come to pick you up
column3: go back into the school office and tell a teacher; do not walk off or accept a lift from someone you were not told about
column4: the school can phone your family and keep you safe until someone arrives

column2: bringing a mobile phone to school
column3: follow the school rule, usually keeping it switched off in your bag or handing it in
column4: phones distract from lessons and many schools allow them only for emergencies

column2: keeping your desk or table tidy
column3: put books, pencils and papers back where they belong at the end of the lesson
column4: you will find things quickly and the room stays safe and pleasant

column3: write in your own words and say where you found the facts
column4: copying text and passing it off as yours is plagiarism, a kind of cheating

column2: disagreeing about how to do a group task
column3: listen to each idea, then vote or try a mix of ideas
column4: fair ways of deciding stop quarrels
